clue.text: Secretary's attempt to make dough

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant, here with the possessive 's

explanation.surface: An office secretary has a go at baking.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is used for its letter: the secretary's attempt reads as PA + S + TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is a flour-and-fat paste, a kind of dough used for pies and tarts.

clue.text: Foppish type to pay a quick call on one who talks foolishly at length

blocks.note: to pop in is to make a brief visit

blocks.clueFragment: on one who talks foolishly at length
blocks.note: a jay is a noisy bird, so the word is used for an impertinent chatterer

explanation.surface: A dandy drops by to see a bore who talks nonsense for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the second piece after the first. Jay for a chatterer is an old usage drawn from the noisy bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, showy person, a dandy fussy about dress, like a fop.

clue.text: Part company in Adriatic port

blocks.note: first meaning: to separate or break up
second meaning: a city on the Croatian coast

explanation.surface: Two travellers go their separate ways at a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is to break up or separate; Split is also Croatia's second city, a harbour on the Dalmatian coast.

clue.text: USA-run lotteries, awfully chancy business

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a messed-up order

explanation.surface: American state lotteries are a very risky game.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is a lethal game of chance with a revolver, and figuratively any reckless gamble.

clue.text: Gemstones in suit

blocks.note: first meaning: precious stones of crystallised carbon
second meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jewels sewn into a smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the precious stones and the red playing-card suit marked with lozenge shapes.

clue.text: List that is full of incorrect times

indicators.note: incorrect means wrong, so the word that follows is put into a wrong order
a thing full of something holds it inside, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A timetable riddled with wrong times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is the standard crossword cue for the abbreviation i.e.; 'List' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set things out item by item, which is what making a list means.

clue.text: "In the Mood" a fiddler rearranged - that's easy listening

indicators.note: rearranged means put into a new order

explanation.surface: A violinist plays an arrangement of the Glenn Miller swing hit 'In the Mood', the very picture of easy listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'In' look like part of the song title, but only the following fifteen letters are shuffled; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road is the music-trade label for unchallenging mainstream pop, much the same as easy listening.

clue.text: Lots again suffering homesickness

indicators.note: suffering letters are in a bad way and get knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Many people are once more pining for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia originally meant acute homesickness, from Greek words for homecoming and pain.

clue.text: One who points out a worthless group of people?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who shows, read as a whimsical agent noun
second meaning: British slang for a useless lot

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a bunch of good-for-nothings.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense makes an agent noun from 'show'; the second is British slang, as in 'what a shower!' for a hopeless bunch. The question mark flags the invented first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows things is jokingly a 'show-er'; in British slang a shower is also a contemptible, incompetent crowd.

clue.text: Free one individual

blocks.note: first meaning: unattached, not in a relationship
second meaning: just one, a lone person or thing

explanation.surface: Releasing a lone prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Single describes someone unmarried and available, and also anything consisting of only one.

clue.text: Drinks drop of tea in wood in the Holy Land

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
the drinks and the drop sit inside the wood, which wraps round them

blocks.note: pine is a type of wood; it goes round the other pieces

explanation.surface: Someone sips beer and tea among the trees in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a verb with 'tea' as its object; it is a plural noun for the beers.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestine is the historical name for the region known in Christian tradition as the Holy Land.

clue.text: Such music is constant during party?

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside its span, so these letters go inside the party word

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics
a do is a party; it goes round the other letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether the music playing non-stop at a party is a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition leans on the rest of the clue: party music is exactly this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of dance music from the 1970s, the kind that plays all night at a party.

clue.text: Tonight, a telling off in a London Tube station

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets a reprimand on the London Underground this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling off' reads as a scolding, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill Gate is a station on the London Underground in west London, serving the Central, Circle and District lines.

clue.text: Musical instruction from an eminent Florentine

blocks.note: Dante Alighieri, the great poet, was born in Florence

explanation.surface: Directions on a score handed down by a famous man from Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is an Italian tempo marking telling performers to play at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Terribly rude urge I suppressed, as required by etiquette

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone stifles an impolite impulse because good manners demand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressed' belongs to the surface only: read cryptically, the shuffled letters are what good form calls for.
explanation.definitionFit: De rigueur is a French borrowing meaning required by custom or fashion, obligatory under the rules of polite society.

clue.text: Sufficient to answer demand in the noughties

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Supply met demand during the first decade of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: Having enough means having as much as is needed, a quantity that meets what is required.

clue.text: Greek hero's trek cut short by us

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an odyssey is a long, eventful journey

explanation.surface: The legendary Greek wanderer's voyage is curtailed by us.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Fittingly, the word for a long trek comes from this hero's own story.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, is the hero of Homer's Odyssey, which tells of his ten-year voyage home from Troy.

clue.text: A service attended by elderly poet

blocks.note: the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: An old poet goes to a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like worship; in crosswords it often means an armed service, here the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian poet, author of 'Dover Beach'.

clue.text: Notice old man in study, poker-faced

indicators.note: these pieces are placed in the room word, which wraps round them

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
a den is a study, a private room for work; it goes round the other pieces

explanation.surface: Spotting an elderly man in his study, keeping a straight face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb; it is a noun, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan means expressionless, showing no emotion, just as a poker player hides any reaction.

clue.text: Lad went swimming in marshy area

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they come back in a different order

explanation.surface: A boy took a dip in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is both part of the fodder and part of the phrase that signals the shuffle; only 'swimming' carries the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wetland is land saturated with water, such as a marsh, swamp or fen.

clue.text: Heading for workshop that is most spacious

indicators.note: a heading comes at the top, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: id est is the Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: A workshop's header boasts it is the roomiest.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'that is' is given in full Latin rather than the usual i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Widest is the superlative of wide, meaning having the greatest breadth, hence the most roomy.

clue.text: French writer penning page in college grounds

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Albert Camus, author of The Outsider; it goes round the other piece
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A French novelist writes a page while at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, which suits the writer; it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Golden sands - name changed in novel

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A beach called Golden Sands is renamed in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels and Demons is a 2000 thriller by Dan Brown, the book that introduced Robert Langdon.

clue.text: Some from a haunted place in Nebraska

indicators.note: some means a portion of what follows, so the letters are part of that run of words

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: Part of a spooky location in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska, on the Missouri River.

clue.text: Gather in place to dine

blocks.note: Pl. is the abbreviation for place in street names

explanation.surface: People assemble somewhere to have dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like a verb for people meeting; it is the sewing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressmaking a pleat is a fold of cloth, and a gather is a similar fold drawn up in fabric.

clue.text: Musical work, formerly spoken start to elegy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Describes a piece of music that once began with a spoken lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical composition evoking rural, shepherding life.

clue.text: Police officer gets near criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A detective closes in on a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank above constable and below inspector.

clue.text: Plans to include large models

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: ideas are plans or schemes; it goes round the other piece
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Designs drawn up to cover big scale models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' looks like miniatures or fashion models; it means perfect examples to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection, things held up as models to imitate.
